messages.content:
You compare an edited output video against its actual source video, the original user request, and the executed editing instruction. Optional reference assets show the desired editing target.
The historical-source selection in the original user request has already been executed. Evaluate only its editing requirements against the actual videos. Do not treat historical appearance descriptions in that request as observed facts; use the visible source video instead. Compare the original editing requirements with the executed instruction too, so you can identify any omitted or changed constraint introduced when the instruction was normalized.
The output_video_card was produced earlier by independently observing only the output. Treat it as a fixed observation record: do not rewrite it, return a new card, or add intended changes to it. It can be imperfect; inspect the actual videos when comparing.
Call record_edit_result exactly once. Return only its five parameters: requested_change, observed_change, fulfillment, unexpected_changes, uncertain. These describe the source-to-output comparison, not a new video card. Use concise English.
State what was requested and what visibly changed. Use fulfillment=fulfilled, partial, not_fulfilled, or uncertain. Do not infer success from the instruction. Note unintended changes to identity, appearance, action, scene, camera, timing, and image quality when visible. If a reference match or subtle facial change cannot be judged, record the uncertainty rather than assuming success. Do not claim to have inspected missing reference pixels. Do not call an editing tool or regenerate video.
Use one separate XML parameter block for each of the five parameters. The three text parameters contain text. unexpected_changes and uncertain contain JSON arrays of strings, including [] when empty. Do not nest a card or review object inside any parameter.
Structural example only; replace descriptions with your actual comparison:
<tool_call>
<function=record_edit_result>
<parameter=requested_change>Requested edit</parameter>
<parameter=observed_change>Actual visible change</parameter>
<parameter=fulfillment>uncertain</parameter>
<parameter=unexpected_changes>[]</parameter>
<parameter=uncertain>["Any unresolved comparison"]</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>

content.text: {"executed_editing_prompt":"Change the video's camera setup to an upper-body shot from behind. Change only the camera setup. Preserve the person's appearance, expression, and action, along with the existing scene. Use the provided camera reference image to determine the viewing direction, subject placement, and framing at the start of the edited video. Follow the described camera setup and movement, and preserve the timing and progression of the action in the source video.","history_selection_status":"Already executed. Only compare editing requirements; historical appearance words are not observed facts.","original_user_request":"Please return to the result of edit 1 and make the following change to that video: Using the provided source video, apply the following edit: I'd like to change the video's camera setup to an upper-body shot from behind. Change only the camera setup. Preserve the person's appearance, expression, and action, along with the existing scene. Use the provided reference image to determine the viewing direction, subject placement, and framing at the start of the edited video. Follow the camera setup and movement described above, and preserve the timing and progression of the action in the source video.","output_video_card":{"observed":{"action":"The person stands facing away from the camera, then turns their body to the right and back, shifting their weight and moving their arms slightly.","camera":"The camera is static, positioned at a medium distance behind the subject, capturing them from the waist up against the background.","clothing":"They are wearing a white sleeveless tank top with thin pink trim and light green shorts.","hair_color":"The hair appears dark brown or black.","hairstyle":"Their hair is pulled up into a high, somewhat messy bun or topknot.","identity":"A person with a medium build and tanned skin is shown from behind, with their face not visible.","scene":"The setting is an outdoor paved area, likely a patio or terrace, overlooking a calm body of water under a clear blue sky."},"uncertain":[]}}

arguments.observed_change: The output begins as a closer upper-body rear view matching the reference framing, then follows the same turning motion as the source. The person's clothing, hairstyle, scene, and action progression remain broadly consistent.
arguments.requested_change: Change only the camera setup to an upper-body shot from behind, using the reference for initial framing, while preserving the person's appearance, action, scene, and timing.
uncertain: Whether the camera movement after the first frame exactly matches the intended reference-driven setup is difficult to verify from the sampled frames.
unexpected_changes: The initial framing is tighter than the source, as requested, but the later portion of the shot appears to return to a wider framing similar to the source.
